findings.title: Practical sovereignty and partner-like security
findings.claim: The refusal reaches practical claims of ownership and future security: wealth can be treated as a partner-like guarantor, while the Lord relation keeps that guarantee from becoming distributed sovereignty.
findings.mechanism: The two focus occurrences of my Lord carry ownership and governance, and the first-person partnership verb names the act of making a partner. The supplied 30:28 ownership analogy places imagined partners inside what Allah provides, so the negation returns through the focus relation to practical attribution.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why the line reaches reliance on wealth and its supports, not only the naming of another deity.
findings.containment: This does not call wealth a deity or forbid ordinary cooperation; it isolates partner-like attribution of security, ownership, or governing power.

epistemic.reason: The trusted cross-run record supplies exact focus anchors and the 30:28 connection supplies a concrete wider ownership trigger; the legacy duplicate is retained as attributed corroboration.

branch_activations.activation: The wider ownership comparison makes contact with both Lord occurrences, so the focus denial can govern attribution of future security rather than only a verbal label.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The speaker refuses to let wealth or its human supports function as a co-owner or co-governor of the future secured by the Lord.
branch_activations.boundary: The activation concerns partner-like attribution of provision and security; it does not make wealth literally divine or erase ordinary human agency.

branch_activations.boundary: This does not exclude every partnership, assistance, or material cause; it excludes their elevation into ultimate co-sovereignty.

findings.title: From association to ultimate attribution
findings.claim: The refusal marks the point at which human association and help would be promoted into independent causal or ultimate partnership.
findings.mechanism: The focus partnership carrier holds both ordinary sharing and the supplied God-partner facet. The 9:31 connection shows human authorities being elevated into rival lords, while the 18:42 retrospective echo names partnership as the pericope's causal error; together they return the wider distinction through the focus verb.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can keep companionship and cooperation in view while seeing why the line reaches responsibility for who or what receives credit for outcomes.
findings.containment: No claim is made that all social plurality is forbidden or that every borderline case is resolved; 9:31 is the wider trigger and 18:42 is retained as attributed retrospective support.

epistemic.reason: The trusted finding supplies the focus carrier, the 9:31 connection supplies an independent wider authority trigger, and legacy reader-walk records preserve the 18:42 echo without being treated as independent lexical proof.

findings.title: Absolute uniqueness behind exhaustive refusal
findings.claim: The final indefinite under negation carries a qualified uniqueness pressure: refusing any associate also preserves the Lord's relation as belonging to one incomparable divine reality.
findings.mechanism: The supplied focus occurrence 18:38:8:1 is the final anyone-carrier under negation. The 112:1 connection supplies an independent occurrence of Allah's absolute oneness and returns that uniqueness through the same focus word, allowing the negative scope to be heard against positive divine singularity.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the final object as more than a numeric one: its exhaustive scope also protects the uniqueness of the one named Lord.
findings.containment: The word remains the indefinite object under negation and is not converted into a positive divine name or numeral; the branch identity is qualified and the connection target has no supplied target morphology.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus occurrence and qualified branch record are supplied, and the 112:1 connection supplies target Arabic plus a focus return. Its prior label is a nomination rather than a decision, so the resonance remains qualified.
